Once upon a time, there was a fierce debate over whether the future of folding smartphones would be flip-style or book-style, but for now at least, the book-style foldable design seems to have won.

Samsung's eighth-generation foldable phone uses this design, the highly anticipated iPhone Ultra is reportedly set to follow suit, and leaked images of the Xiaomi 18 Fold also appear to point in the same direction...

There are two main body designs for folding smartphones, generally referred to as clamshell and book-style.

The clamshell design essentially folds a traditional smartphone in half, resulting in a device with increased thickness but halved height, offering a standard-sized screen in a more portable form. The Motorola Razr is one such example, and this design is reminiscent of the model the company first launched back in 2004.

The book-style design (increasingly named as such for obvious reasons) is a more square-shaped device that unfolds into a small tablet roughly the size of an iPad mini. This is the design Apple plans to unveil next month.

Samsung popularised this design with its Galaxy Z Fold series, and the model launched last month has already reached its eighth generation.

Xiaomi is also preparing to join the fray with the 18 Fold, whose camera module design bears some resemblance to the anticipated iPhone Ultra. Weibo user Peter shared two photos (above), which he believes are engineering test units rather than actual production models.

Our sister site 9to5Google noted that this deep cherry colour seems to reference one of the rumoured colour options for the iPhone 18 Pro.
